claims.text: Increasing chloride ion concentration destabilizes the nascent oxide film on pre-exposure Q235 steel.
Lowering solution pH destabilizes the nascent oxide film on pre-exposure Q235 steel.
Oxide-film destabilization causes earlier corrosion onset and accelerated corrosion at approximately 25 °C and 200 °C.
Lower chloride concentration and near-neutral pH promote formation of a more protective oxide that delays corrosion initiation.
The proposed initial material consists of freshly polished, degreased, uncoated Q235 steel coupons with no prior exposure.
The controlled study will vary chloride concentration from 0 to 5 wt.% and pH from 2 to 10 while controlling oxygen content.
Comparing tests at approximately 25 °C and 200 °C will isolate temperature-driven effects on oxide stability.
All tests will use aqueous solutions with controlled oxygen levels and agitation.
Uncoated Q235 steel in neutral solution at 25 °C will serve as the reference.
Formation and breakdown of an initially protective oxide or passivation layer is the structural mediator governing corrosion onset.
High chloride concentration and low pH cause local oxide breakdown that facilitates pitting and general corrosion.
Elevated temperature magnifies chloride- and acidity-driven oxide breakdown and corrosion.
Milder solution conditions stabilize the passivation layer and retard corrosion onset.
Pitting onset will occur earlier and total corrosion rate will rise as chloride concentration increases and pH decreases relative to the reference.
Near-neutral or basic solutions will produce delayed corrosion initiation and lower mass loss because oxide-film breakdown is slower.
Near-neutral, low-chloride conditions at room temperature will cause minimal corrosion because an intact protective oxide remains on uncoated Q235 steel.
The predictions may not apply above 200 °C, beyond two weeks of immersion, or in the presence of untested contaminants.
Corrosion initiation, polarization resistance, mass loss, and pitting density can be tracked to test the proposed dependence on chloride, pH, and temperature.
